name: acad-lisp
description: AutoLISP evaluation, AutoCAD command sequences, system variables and module loading - the escape hatches and the settings layer. eval_lisp reaches anything AutoCAD exposes to LISP but this bank has no dedicated tool for, and it returns the expression's REAL VALUE rather than an acknowledgement, because every route in this category is synchronous: Application.Invoke for LISP, Editor.Command for command sequences and scripts, and Application.Get/SetSystemVariable for settings. SendCommand-style queuing is deliberately not used anywhere here - a result that cannot be observed is not a result. Also here: loading .lsp files and .NET assemblies, listing what is loaded, reading and writing system variables with the value read back afterwards, and purging unreferenced registered application names. Command aliases are NOT here: AutoCAD exposes no API for them and the only route would be editing the global acad.pgp. Prefer a dedicated tool from another category where one exists - they validate arguments and verify their own results - and reach for eval_lisp or run_command_sequence when none does.
intent_examples: batch some commands from a file

drive a command from the command line

tools_summary.name: eval_lisp
tools_summary.description: Evaluate an AutoLISP expression and return its REAL VALUE - not an acknowledgement that something ran. This is the escape hatch: anything AutoCAD exposes to AutoLISP is reachable here, including functions a .lsp file has already defined with load_lisp_file. Runs via a queued command-line evaluation that writes its result to a file and this waits for it (rule 26 §15/§24) - synchronous from the caller's point of view. nil comes back as null, T as true, and a list keeps its nesting; `printed` carries what LISP itself printed alongside the parsed value, for results with no JSON equivalent (an ename, a selection set). A syntax error or an undefined function name is refused with LISP's own error message rather than returned as a plausible-looking nil.
intent: eval this lisp and give me the result
oblicz wyrazenie lispa i podaj wynik
escape hatch for something with no tool

tools_summary.name: get_system_variable
tools_summary.description: Read one AutoCAD system variable by name - CLAYER, OSMODE, INSUNITS and the rest. Read-only. Read straight from Application.GetSystemVariable rather than through LISP. The value comes back as text with its underlying CLR type named alongside, because a system variable can hold a string, an integer, a real or a point, and set_system_variable has to be given the matching one. An unknown name is refused rather than answered with an empty value; list_system_variables gives the ones this bank knows by name.
intent: what is the current layer variable

tools_summary.name: list_loaded_applications
tools_summary.description: List the ARX, CRX and DBX modules AutoCAD has registered, together with its own managed core assemblies (accoremgd.dll, acmgd.dll). Read-only. MEASURED LIMIT, so that a short answer is not mistaken for a broken tool: this returns what DynamicLinker.GetLoadedModules reports, which on a normal session is about 25 entries and does NOT include .NET assemblies loaded with NETLOAD - a netloaded plugin will not appear here even though it is running. `pattern` filters the list by substring.
intent: show the loaded arx and dbx modules
jak sprawdzic zaladowane moduly na rysunku

tools_summary.name: list_loaded_lisp
tools_summary.description: List the AutoLISP symbols currently defined - from (atoms-family 1), the only enumeration AutoCAD actually offers. Read-only. IMPORTANT: these are SYMBOLS, not files - AutoCAD keeps no record of which .lsp files were loaded, so this is the honest answer to 'what LISP is loaded', not a file list. Built-in functions are included alongside anything a .lsp defined, which is why a fresh drawing already answers with hundreds and `pattern` matters. Names starting C: are the ones that can be typed at the command line, listed separately as commandSymbols.
intent: show lisp commands defined by a loaded file

tools_summary.name: list_system_variables
tools_summary.description: List the system variables worth knowing, grouped by what they affect - drafting aids, current properties, text and dimensions, units, display, 3D, file state and plotting - each with its live value and type. Read-only. `pattern` filters by name or by group. IMPORTANT: this is a CURATED list, not a complete one - AutoCAD exposes no way to enumerate system variables, there being no table to walk - so treat it as a starting point rather than a boundary: any variable not listed still works with get_system_variable and set_system_variable. Every value is read live rather than remembered, so a name this build of AutoCAD does not have is counted as not present instead of being reported with a stale value.

tools_summary.name: load_lisp_file
tools_summary.description: Load an AutoLISP (.lsp) file, making its functions available for eval_lisp to call. Does not search the support path - give the full path. Returns the value of the LAST expression in the file, which for a file of defuns is usually the name of the last one defined; that is the closest thing to a confirmation the loader offers, so to be sure a particular function arrived, call it with eval_lisp - an undefined name is an error there, not a silent nil.
intent: load an autolisp routine from disk

tools_summary.name: purge_regapps
tools_summary.description: Remove unreferenced registered application names from the drawing. Registered app names are the keys extended data is filed under, and they accumulate in a drawing that has passed through several applications. Only the UNREFERENCED ones go: Database.Purge is asked first and strikes from the candidate list everything still in use, so a name that some xdata still points at is kept - erasing one that is referenced would corrupt that xdata. ACAD is AutoCAD's own and is never offered. Reports the names purged and the ones remaining, with the counts before and after.
intent: purge the drawing of stale app names

tools_summary.name: run_command_sequence
tools_summary.description: Run ONE AutoCAD command with its answers, one token each - for example ["_.CIRCLE", "0,0", "10"]. Underscore-dot prefixes keep it working on a non-English AutoCAD and immune to a redefined command name. Runs in a genuine COMMAND context (rule 26 §15) via a queued [CommandMethod], NOT the application context every other tool in this bank dispatches from - Editor.Command throws from there. TWO MEASURED LIMITS, both refused rather than silently wrong: a second command chained after the first in one call is dropped without error, so only one command per call is accepted; and commands that prompt for object SELECTION (ERASE, MOVE, COPY and similar - not an exhaustive list) complete and report success while changing nothing, so the common ones are refused by name. Commands that only draw new geometry (CIRCLE, LINE, RECTANG, PLINE, ...) work reliably. Editor.Command returns VOID, so the count of model-space entities before and after is the evidence this tool can honestly report. A sequence that runs out of answers leaves AutoCAD waiting for one it will never get - this tool then TIMES OUT rather than hanging forever, and says to check the AutoCAD window, because it cannot see what is on screen.
intent: drive a command from the command line
run this autocad command with answers

tools_summary.name: set_system_variable
tools_summary.description: Set one AutoCAD system variable - setvar. The value is converted to the type the variable already holds, since passing a string to an integer variable is rejected outright. The new value is READ BACK afterwards and the tool refuses if it did not change: a read-only system variable accepts the call and quietly keeps its old value, which would otherwise be indistinguishable from success. Both the previous and the new value are reported, so a change can be undone by setting the old one back.
